results.name: Guardians without a kit keep no tiers; a kit guardian turns at two thirds and one third of its health
A credited seed stops at a threshold and the next is guarded; powers and uncredited strikes pass it
The mood change is a 1.3 s guarded warning, then Phase Bloom: the next tier, a beat of rest, faster moves
A guardian dropped past both thresholds at once changes one mood per warning
Kit timers and lob flights keep the guardian clock: a Lullaby holds them
A beaten kit guardian leaves nothing behind: no moon gates, carried flowers, timers or raised line
bosses.js never touches the seed pod and never uses Math.random
Old Sunny: a power that reaches a portal or the snooze Z blooms it but takes no rings off him
Old Sunny: turning Cranky at two-thirds health and Wide awake at a third, each mood opening on its new move, with his own words for each
Old Sunny: a credited seed stops at his first mood line and the stage is announced next tick; his portals can still be shot
Old Sunny: the change to Cranky is a guarded 1.3 s warning, then Phase Bloom, a dizzy Sunny stays dizzy, and he yawns next
Old Sunny: a yawn drops the volley and opens a sun portal above each sprout; each spits one more 1.6 s later, then closes
Old Sunny: shutting a portal stops its spit and pays exactly one more sun than a plain part bloom; uncredited pays nothing
Old Sunny: a yawn never cuts short a dizzy window, and a portal is dropped where a flower is in its way
Old Sunny: the snooze Z drifts from beside his face to just above the launcher; landing naps the aim guide only
Old Sunny: popping the Z wakes him dizzy for 3 s (his nap bubble goes too); double hits still stop at a threshold
Old Sunny: from Cranky on his nap bubble takes two hits; Sleepy keeps the one-hit bubble
Old Sunny: the bot ranks a portal about to spit at 70, the Z at 80, and his bubble still first
Old Sunny: tier 2 plays the same at 30, 60 and 144 FPS
Old Sunny: a Lullaby holds the portals, their spit and the Z in flight; they carry on after it, late by its length
Old Sunny: his moods, portals, Z and napping aim guide draw balanced, finite and with no per-frame gradients
Old Sunny: beaten mid-attack, he leaves no portal, Z, timer or napping aim guide behind
Rootknot turns Tangled at two-thirds health and Furious at a third, each mood opening on its new move; every warning fits a phone
A credited seed stops Rootknot at each mood line; the change is announced, then Tangled opens with the carousel and Furious with the snare
He comes up at holes 292, 128 and 210 in turn; Grumpy, every other burrow lobs a rolypoly that lands as a real one at +.6 s
Tangled, he lobs two (.18 s apart); a blocked hole stays quiet, a drifted flower moves a landing aside, and four is the most
Bowled over: a rolypoly rolled into Rootknot deals 3 with a critical, never while he is underground, and stops at the mood line
Tangled, the Root Carousel takes the biggest clump round a 30 px ring that sinks with the descent, evenly spaced, as forecast
Left alone, the carousel flings its flowers 40 px outward at 3.5 s; they fall 1.3x for 2 s. Furious it spins 7 s, or less near the line
With no clump to take he roots up three seedlings of his own on a clear ring and spins them; a seedling spot filled during the tell is a short rest
Snap the knot (two hits) and its flowers bloom in a cascade credited within .4 s; shot singly they leave the ring; the bot wants the knot
Furious, the Root Snare blocks the busier side of the fan for 4 s: 82 px at y 405.65 and 35°, never below 430
Rootknot plays the same at 30, 60 and 144 FPS
A Lullaby holds his lobs, carousel and snare where they are; each lands, flings or withers late by its length
Beaten mid-move, Rootknot leaves nothing behind: no carried flowers, knot, lobs, timers, snare or hurried falls
The good bot beats Rootknot
Rootknot's art draws every move, Animations on and off, with no gradient or blur per frame; his three moods are three faces
Mother Morel: turning Tricky at two-thirds health and Stormy at a third, each mood opening on its new move, with her own words for each
Mother Morel: a credited puff chain one above a threshold stops on it and the stage is announced next tick; an uncredited one passes
Mother Morel: Tricky and Stormy are each a guarded 1.3 s warning, then Phase Bloom and the new list
Mother Morel: her waltz partner circles her at 58 px for 8 s, forecast exactly, then twirls home quietly
Mother Morel: popping her partner chains into her for 2 with a "waltz" critical, and stops at a threshold
Mother Morel: a fakeout tosses one real puffcap and two fibcaps to three spots, landing 0.9 s later
Mother Morel: a fakeout spot filled during the warning gets no cap; the start ring shows the kept spots and one is still real
Mother Morel: wherever her sway has carried her, every cap shown in the fakeout lands, the spotted one included
Mother Morel: her bonnet marks no puffcap beside her while her waltz partner is still dancing, and adds none
Mother Morel: ink rain drops from three lanes for 4 s, 15 drops in all, each its own group
Mother Morel: the painted waltz paints all but one partner into fibcaps at 2.3 s; a direct hit sneezes and shuts her bonnet
Mother Morel: tier 2 plays the same at 30, 60 and 144 FPS
Mother Morel: a Lullaby holds the dance, the tossed caps and the rain; each carries on after it, late by its length
Mother Morel: beaten mid-dance, mid-toss and mid-rain, she leaves no partner, lob, timer or raised line behind
Mother Morel: her moods, partners, paint, tosses and ink rain draw balanced, finite and with no per-frame gradients
Crystal Heart: longer-lived than her old 36; a credited touch shatters a fake into two coral shards, no damage, and it re-forms 2.0 s later
Crystal Heart: no shards while six are loose; powers and credited chains never pop a fake; a script pops one quietly
Crystal Heart stops at her first mood line: the held real heart turns seeds away while a fake still shatters; a mirror shot clamps too
Crystal Heart turns Shining, then Racing, each with its own words; Shining opens with the shuffle
Mirror Shards open below the sunken guardian and her hearts, and she rests instead when that row would crowd the line
Mirror Shards: two blades at y 356 hold still .8 s, turn .7 rad each second, freeze in a Lullaby and leave after 6 s
A seed banked off a mirror into the real heart is a Mirror shot: two damage, a critical, a flash; a late one is plain
Heartbeat Hues: the real heart wants one of the next three seeds; other colors glance off and the bot holds them
Crystal Heart replays identically at 30, 60 and 144 FPS, and a strike loop leaves nothing behind
Lantern Lily turns Glowing at two-thirds health and Moonlit at a third, each mood opening on its new move; every warning fits a phone; she still opens with her whirlpool
A credited seed stops Lily at her first mood line; while the change is announced her lantern is held (it stays lit), a pad can still be shot
Moon Gate: a low moon on the lake and a high one over her, both legal tunnel mouths, for 5 s of her clock
Moon shot: a seed shot straight into the low moon drops onto her top for two, a critical; touched or late, it is a plain hit
Lily Pads: two pads open low on the lake; each sends up a moon jelly at +.9 s and +2.1 s, then sinks at +2.6 s
Shooting a pad shut stops its jellies and pays exactly one more sun than a plain part bloom; uncredited pays nothing
Glowworm Lantern: her lantern crawls off as a glowworm's head, 70 px below her at x 300 (else 100); no room, the tide comes
Hit the worm's head: the light runs home, three damage, her gutter open at +.2 s and closed at +5.3 s; it clamps at a mood line
Left alone for 7 s the worm puffs away, pieces split off it too, with no life lost; the lantern floats home lit
Rising Tide: the line rises up to 28 px over .6 s, holds until the recede at 5.6 s and is back at 448 by 6.4 s
The tide never rises to within 18 px of a piece that would cost a life (glowdrops and worms too); jellies do not count
Lily plays the same at 30, 60 and 144 FPS
A Lullaby holds her clock: moons, pad jellies, the worm's puffback and the tide all wait, then carry on late by its length
Beaten mid-move, Lily leaves nothing behind: no moons, pads, worm, timers or raised line, and her lantern back on its stem
Lily's art draws every move, Animations on and off, with no gradient or blur per frame; her three moods are three faces
The good bot beats Lantern Lily
Ember Rose: 100 health with moods at 67 and 34, three moods, her familiar dive first, and every word fits
Ember Rose: a seed into her flame spits a cinder you can catch for a sun; a missed one cools to a coal that rolls off tunnel mouths
Ember Rose: her fire rings hide her and land her at the far ring; a ring shot deals 3, and at Blazing a level tunnel is too hot
Ember Rose: three castanet clicks, then the stomp shoves flowers 16 px (never past line - 70, never up, never into each other) and Olé opens her
Ember Rose: an Olé hit that brings on her next mood keeps her standing still until Olé ends
Ember Rose: the wave hint keeps up with her moods (tunnels hit triple only while Flickering)
Ember Rose: a Lullaby holds Olé, a falling cinder and her dive
Ember Rose: her barrage sows three whizzbangs in one swaying group, and one lit under her deals 3
Ember Rose: the same fight at 30, 60 and 144 FPS
Ember Rose: beaten mid-ring, mid-Olé or right after a barrage, she leaves no ring, coal, cinder or rocket behind
Ember Rose's art draws every move, Animations on and off, with no gradient or blur per frame; her three moods are three faces
